Chief Executive’s Foreword 
 
As ever, it is a busy time here in Fingal as we enter the 
summer season and look forward to the many events 
which will be taking place across the county. One such 
annual event is Bike Week which takes place this year from 
Saturday, 9th May to Sunday, 17th May. As always, there is 
an exciting, fun and family friendly programme of events in 
store starting off with the Fingal Climate Action & Bike 
Week Family Fun Day in Millennium Park, Blanchardstown 
on Saturday, 9th May. Visitors to Millennium Park from 
12pm – 6pm will enjoy street velodrome, archery, street 
games, free bike repair, the Turning Tides pop‑up sea 
aquarium and activities from the Dublin 15 Toy Library. 
Bremore Castle Family Fun Day on Saturday 16th May from 
11am–4pm will offer bike safety checks, street games and 
the popular Fireride Cycling Skills Course, encouraging 
confident and safe cycling in a fun and supportive 
environment. Malahide Castle Family Fun Day takes place 
on Sunday 17th May from 11am–6pm and there will be 
something for everyone of all ages with a pop‑up BMX skills 
track, free bike repair, street games, Cycling Without Age 
trishaw 
rides, 
pedal‑powered 
cycling 
games, 
bike 
orienteering and outdoor movie screenings. Bike Week is 
funded by the National Transport Authority (NTA) and 
delivered locally by Fingal’s Active Travel Unit and is a 
celebration of cycling as a healthy, sustainable and fun 
mode of transport. Throughout Bike Week, there are a 
huge number of activities catering for beginners to more 
experienced cyclists including historical cycling tours, 
school workshops, the sunset cycle and the pedal parade. 
You can plan your bike week by checking out all the 
wonderful events here: Bike Week 2026 | Fingal County 
Council  
 
I am pleased that Explore Fingal Markets are running this 
year following a very successful pilot in 2025. Swords 
Castle, the Casino Model Railway Museum in Malahide and 
Millennium Park, Blanchardstown are the locations for the 
markets which run throughout the summer months. We 
have a proud tradition of food production in Fingal and the 
markets are the ideal place to obtain fresh, locally sourced 
food and drink as well as a huge array of artisan products. 
Fingal Food Circle and Fingal Farmers will be well 
represented at the markets with stallholders showcasing 
their delicious range of produce. You can find out more 
about the markets, and all the other gems that Fingal has 
to offer, on the recently launched Explore Fingal website 
Markets - Explore Fingal 
 
Last month, Mr Raffaele Fitto, European Commission 
Executive Vice-President for Cohesion and Reforms, visited 
Fingal to see the progress on Swords Cultural Quarter.  
 
 
Mr. Fitto was given a guided tour of Swords Castle and the 
Carnegie Library and viewed the ongoing work on Culture 
House which will be a phenomenal addition to the cultural 
and artistic fabric of the town once completed in 2027. 
Development works at Swords Castle and Carnegie Library 
received a grant from the European Regional Development 
Fund (ERDF). A sum of approximately €1.5 million was 
secured in ERDF funding under the Southern & Eastern 
Regional Operational Programme which Fingal County 
Council funding matched to facilitate conservation and 
improvement works at Swords Castle and a refurbishment 
project at Carnegie Library. Together with the Mayor of 
Fingal, Cllr Tom O’Leary, I was pleased to have the 
opportunity to welcome the Executive Vice President to 
Fingal to see the transformation of this area which 
promises to serve as a socially and culturally vibrant space 
for future generations. 
 
There was a decidedly jovial atmosphere at County Hall on 
Wednesday, 29th April when a brand-new minibus was 
presented to St. Michael’s House (SMH) Oaklands Service, 
Swords. I was delighted to have made the presentation on 
behalf of the staff of Fingal County Council who committed 
to raising €31,665 over the past three years to enable the 
purchase. The Oaklands Service provides vital supports for 
adults with intellectual and physical disabilities which 
enables clients to live independently and with autonomy 
over life decisions. A reliable and comfortable means of 
transport ensures ease of transfer to appointments or 
social outings within the community and we hope that this 
new minibus will be utilised and enjoyed by the many 
clients and service users of St. Michael’s House. 
 
Finally, the upcoming Howth Maritime & Seafood Festival 
guarantees to be a fantastic weekend of fun, crafts, music, 
live entertainment and, of course, delicious seafood. 
Taking place from the evening of Friday 22nd May and on 
Saturday 23rd & Sunday 24th May 2026 from 12-6pm daily, 
Howth Harbour will be a hive of activity with family friendly 
activities, live music and irresistible delicacies to try. Howth 
is a place that is synonymous with stunning vistas, vibrant 
local businesses and the freshest catches straight from the 
sea. I hope you can take the opportunity to drop by and 
enjoy a very pleasant visit. 
 
Best wishes, 
AnnMarie Farrelly 
Chief Executive

The Heritage Properties team received the very sad

passed away at home at his UK home.   Alec was a 
renowned Artist, Art collector, Restorer and interior 
fabrics advisor in his own right. He was known to the 
local community in Donabate and within the Local

House. His reputation was as a warm host and light-
hearted man, He was generous and light-hearted 
towards all the Council staff who got to know him and 
very willing to share his family legacy and stories.  
May he rest in peace.

Ballough Place Artist Residential Studio 
 
 
Fingal Arts Office, in partnership with Beet, Woad and 
Rust, held a natural plant dyeing workshop at 
Ballough Place Artist Residential Studio on Saturday 
28th March from 2.30pm. 
  
This new residential artist studio, as part of the 
Ballough Place development, is a pioneering initiative 
by Fingal County Council to provide a secure, high 
quality live/workspace for a professional visual artist.  
  
Reem and Hugh, from Beet, Woad and Rust, have 
been commissioned by Fingal Arts Office to design 
and implement the interior fit out of the residential 
studio. As part of the commission, they will facilitate 
a series of workshops for Ballough Place residents 
and the local community.  
  
The first workshop focused on natural dyeing using 
Woad, a plant that has been grown for millennia to 
produce Indigo. It is accepted traditionally as a Celtic 
colour, but was also used by the Egyptians, Chinese 
and everyone in between. During the industrial 
revolution it was grown intensively near centers of 
textile production. In North Fingal, once a booming 
textile hub, Woad still grows wildly. 
 
With over 15 people in attendance, this workshop 
was an important opportunity for the local 
community to see the studio space, meet fellow 
residents, and learn new skills.

Preventing Homelessness, Notices to Quit and 
Tenant In-situ Acquisitions  
Fingal County Council is aware that households in the 
Fingal area who may have received a notice to quit, 
which is also referred to as a notice of termination, 
from their landlord may be worried or unsure of 
what to do.  
 
Fingal County Council and the Dublin Regional 
Homeless Executive (DRHE) would like to advise 
anyone affected of the services that are available to 
them in these circumstances.  
 
Page 72 
We strongly encourage tenants residing in the 
Fingal area, who have been issued with a notice 
of termination, to contact Fingal County Council 
as soon as they receive a notice from their 
landlord. The contact details for Fingal County 
Council are provided at the bottom of this page.  
When the tenants contact Fingal County Council, staff 
in the Housing Department will take note of the 
termination date.  
 
The Council advises the tenant to refer the notice to 
Threshold, a service funded by the DRHE to provide 
a Tenancy Protection Service for private renters in 
the Dublin Region, including Fingal. Threshold can 
also be contacted directly on Freephone 1800 454 
454 or via their website www.threshold.ie which 
contains more information and advice on the validity 
of your notice.  
 
The Council’s first response will be to try to prevent 
homelessness. This includes assessing the person’s 
position on the social housing list, providing advice 
on applying for Choice Based Lettings, and advising 
the person on the level of Housing Assistance 
Payment (HAP) they may be eligible to receive. 
  
Placement in emergency accommodation will be a 
last resort if no other alternative can be identified.   
 Fingal County Council continues to liaise with other 
Dublin and neighboring local authorities to deal with 
tenancy issues that may require an inter-authority 
approach.  In particular, we are working closely with 
our colleagues in the other Dublin Local Authorities 
on the implementation of the Government policy and 
guidance, with a focus on the needs of tenants.   
  
Whilst the Council will, in the context of current 
circumstances, adopt flexibility in dealing with 
potential acquisitions of properties with tenants in 
situ, any acquisition is subject to appropriate due 
diligence and checks before any commitment is 
made to acquire, including, for example, determining 
that a valid notice of termination is in place, the 
tenant has a social housing need, and the condition 
and valuation of the property.

The Government has put forward options to allow 
tenants who are not eligible for social housing to 
remain in their homes, including schemes to support 
the purchase of homes and a Cost Rental in-situ 
Scheme. The Cost Rental Tenant-in-Situ Scheme is 
available for tenants who are not eligible for social 
housing and are at risk of homelessness. The DHLGH 
has advised that local authorities are to be the first 
point of contact for this scheme, but it is managed by 
the Housing Agency.  
 
Under the scheme, the Housing Agency can purchase 
a property and rent it to the tenant. Fingal County 
Council will undertake an initial assessment of the 
tenant’s circumstances and refer details to the 
Housing Agency for consideration, where the tenant 
is at risk of homelessness and the Cost Rental 
Tenant-in-Situ scheme applies. The Housing Agency 
will then contact the landlord about the purchase of 
the property.  
  
Where a tenant wishes to purchase their home from 
the landlord, local authorities can provide advice 
about the Local Authority Home Loan scheme. The 
Government is examining implementing a ‘right of 
first refusal’ for tenants to purchase their homes, as 
well as expanding the First Home shared equity 
scheme. The Council will be able to provide more 
information on these when available.  
  
Works around preventing homelessness, assessing 
notices of termination, and responding to tenant and 
landlord in-situ queries are being led on by the 
Council’s Homelessness section, taking a tenant-
centred approach, supported by staff dedicated to 
dealing with tenant in-situ housing acquisitions.

Deposit Return Scheme 
 
Ireland's Deposit Return Scheme (DRS), operated by 
Re-turn, is a circular economy initiative which was 
launched on February 1, 2024, to increase recycling 
rates for plastic bottles and aluminium cans to over 
90%.  
Page 89 
The initiative aims to address the environmental 
challenges posed by single-use bottles & containers. 
It is estimated that 1.9 billion drinks bottles and cans 
are consumed each year in Ireland, in-house and 'on 
the go'. The Deposit Return Scheme aims to boost 
the recycling rate for these drinks containers by 
charging a small, refundable deposit for each plastic 
bottle or can. The Scheme includes PET plastic bottles 
and aluminium and steel cans between 150ml and 3 
litres. A deposit of 15c will apply to containers 500mls 
or less and a deposit of 25c for each container above 
500ml. The Separate Return Scheme (Deposit Return 
Scheme) Regulations 2024 provides a regulatory 
framework for the responsible recycling of in-scope 
bottles and containers. 
 
Monitoring compliance with the Separate Collection 
(Deposit Return Scheme) Regulations 2024, is an 
enforcement responsibility of the Local Authority 
Sector. All producers, retailers and distributors who 
place in- scope products on the market must register 
with the Deposit Return Scheme to fulfil their 
legislative and environmental responsibilities. 
The WERLA and Re-Turn have provided a list of 13

Post-Occupancy Evaluation of Retrofitted Social 
Housing 
The Architects department are undertaking a Post 
Occupancy Evaluation project of retrofitted social 
housing. The purpose of this project is to measure 
the energy performance of 3 dwellings over a 12-
month period, after initial occupancy, and to provide 
a list of recommendations to the social housing 
tenants for reducing energy consumption based on 
their actual consumption.  The project will be the first 
of its kind for the FCC Architects and Housing 
Departments, 
combining 
Quantitative 
and 
Qualitative Data by integrating smart meter readings 
and indoor air quality monitoring with tenant 
feedback surveys to provide a holistic view of 
building performance and the occupant experience. 
It will establish an innovative feedback loop 
comparing the predicted assessment (based on 
DEAP/ BER) and actual performance, informing 
future retrofit strategies and improving the tenant 
experience. 
  
Pilot Project - 30-32 North Street, Swords 
A pilot project for the post occupancy evaluation 
(POE) of 3 No. dwellings within a social housing 
development of 13 homes at 30-32 North St., 
currently 
under 
construction. 
The 
housing 
development comprises renovating two, existing 
vacant, 19th-century dwellings and adding a rear 
extension to regenerate a prominent brownfield site 
in Swords town. The two vacant dwellings are 
undergoing a full thermal retrofit and are being 
converted into 3 homes, which will be the subject of 
this post occupancy evaluation.  
 
Expected Outputs  
By 
combining 
real-world 
data 
with 
occupant 
experience, the findings will directly support FCC’s 
Climate Action Plan 2024 under the headings of 
‘Energy & Buildings’ and ‘Community Engagement’, 
enabling 
smarter, 
more 
sustainable 
housing 
interventions.  
 
Page 94 
The outputs will include:  
 
•Quantitative Data: Energy consumption from 
smart meter readings, indoor air quality monitors 
(temperature, humidity, CO₂ levels) and radon 
monitors collected over 12 months.   
 
•Qualitative Insights: Tenant feedback on thermal 
comfort, energy costs, lighting, heating and hot water 
systems and ease of usability through structured 
surveys.  
 
•Performance Gap Analysis: A comparison of 
predicted 
energy 
performance 
(DEAP/BER 
assessments) versus actual in-use performance, 
identifying areas for improvement.  
 
•Actionable Recommendations: Under Climate 
Action C9 pg98 of the action plan, the project will 
Increase Energy Awareness by providing practical 
guidance for tenants to reduce energy consumption. 
Under Climate Action C23 Pg99, information gathered, 
will provide an opportunity to embed climate 
awareness and enhance future project delivery.  
 
Project Timeline  
30-32 North Street is due for completion Q1 2027. 
Smart meters, radon and indoor air quality monitors 
will be installed prior to handover. The project 
aspects will be discussed with tenants at allocation 
and induction stage. Monitoring will commence once 
the homes are occupied. Data Collection will take 12 
months. An occupant survey will be provided for the 
tenants to fill in at the end of this period. Findings will 
be collated in a report, and recommendations will be 
issued to tenants on completion.
